title: markdown-db v0: typed corpora that live together in one vault (revision 2: tested)
summary: Revision 2 after testing in Obsidian 1.12.7, Astro 7.4.5 and Nuxt Content 3.16.2. Links inside a corpus become relative Markdown links, because they keep a corpus byte-identical wherever it is mounted. Wikilinks stay accepted, never canonical.

blocks.title: The problem and the constraints
blocks.text:
We want to keep facts, such as how coding-agent harnesses behave, as a **corpus**: a folder of typed records that people browse and edit as plain files, and tools validate.

Constraints:

- **Pure data.** The corpus holds only records, schemas and one small root file. Every rule a tool enforces is written in the corpus or in the spec, never only in code. Schemas are JSON Schema 2020-12, not Zod or Rust types.
- **Browsable.** File names read as what they are (`Claude Code.md`), in Finder, on GitHub and in Obsidian.
- **Many corpora in one vault.** Several corpora can sit anywhere in one Obsidian vault, nested at any depth, beside ordinary notes. Moving a corpus must not break links into or out of it.
- **Links that work everywhere.** A reference must resolve the same in our validator and in Obsidian.

The prior art survey found **mdbase** (mdbase-dev/mdbase-spec) closest. We borrow its path and collision rules. We do not adopt its link resolution: mdbase resolves from each collection's root and treats every nested collection as a closed world, so links across corpora break there.

**What changed in revision 2.** We tested the proposal in real tools. In Obsidian, moving a corpus that uses wikilinks rewrote the corpus's own files with vault paths (`[[Archive/2026/harness-reference/harnesses/Claude Code]]`), so the corpus stopped being portable. With relative Markdown links the corpus files did not change at all. Site generators confirmed it: Docusaurus, VitePress and MkDocs follow relative `.md` links natively, and none follows wikilinks without a plugin. So links inside a corpus are now relative Markdown links.

blocks.title: The example vault
blocks.text:
my-vault/
├── .obsidian/
├── markdown-db.md                   corpus "my-vault" (front page)
├── projects/
│   ├── projects.schema.json         type "projects"
│   └── Skillwright.md
├── Daily/
│   └── 2026-11-05.md
├── Notes/
│   └── Claude Code.md               unrelated note, same name (the trap)
└── Research/
    ├── harness-reference/
    │   ├── markdown-db.md           corpus "harness-reference" (front page)
    │   └── harnesses/
    │       ├── harnesses.schema.md     type "harnesses" (optional)
    │       ├── Antigravity CLI.md
    │       ├── Claude Code.md
    │       └── google/
    │           └── Gemini CLI.md    records may sit at any depth
    └── skill-catalog/
        ├── markdown-db.yaml         corpus "skill-catalog" (data-only form)
        └── skills/
            ├── skills.schema.json
            └── deploy.yaml

steps.title: A corpus is a folder holding `markdown-db.md` (or `.yaml` / `.json`)
steps.summary: The vault root is itself a corpus here, named `my-vault`. It owns `projects/`.
steps.detail: The marker's file name alone identifies a corpus. Its data (the spec version, later `depends`) sits in the frontmatter of `markdown-db.md`, or in the whole file for `.yaml` / `.json`. In the `.md` form the body is the corpus's front page, visible in Obsidian. Exactly one marker per folder. A corpus's **name is its folder name**.

steps.title: Nested corpora own their own subtree
steps.summary: A folder with its own root file is a separate corpus. The parent stops at it.
steps.detail: `my-vault` does not own anything under `Research/harness-reference/` or `Research/skill-catalog/`. **Ownership** decides which schema checks a record. It does not limit **resolution**: links resolve across the whole vault (see the resolution ladder).

steps.title: A type is a folder holding its own schema
steps.summary: A folder holding `<its name>.schema.*` is a type. Other folders are free-form narrative.
steps.detail:
The schema is named after its folder: `harnesses/harnesses.schema.md` (or `.yaml` / `.json`), so search and the quick switcher find it by the type name. A folder holding `<its name>.schema.*` is a type; any other folder is free-form narrative. An empty schema makes an untyped type.

Records may sit at any depth below the type folder (`google/Gemini CLI.md`). Ids are file names and stay unique within the type.

steps.title: Files outside any type folder are left alone
steps.summary: Daily notes belong to the vault, not to a type. The validator ignores them.
steps.detail: The same holds for `README.md` inside a corpus. People can keep any notes around a corpus without the validator complaining.

steps.title: Types can use YAML or JSON records
steps.detail: One extension per type. Obsidian does not open these files, so only `validate` checks their links.

blocks.title: What the files say
blocks.text:
# Research/harness-reference/markdown-db.md
---
markdown-db: 0
---
Facts about how coding-agent harnesses behave. Start with [the harnesses](harnesses/harnesses.schema.md).

# Research/harness-reference/harnesses/harnesses.schema.json  (excerpt)
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "Harness",
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": ["vendor", "status"],
  "properties": {
    "vendor":    { "type": "string" },
    "status":    { "enum": ["current", "sunsetting", "retired"] },
    "successor": { "type": "string", "x-ref": "harnesses" }
  }
}

# Research/harness-reference/harnesses/google/Gemini CLI.md
---
vendor: Google
status: sunsetting
successor: "[Antigravity CLI](../Antigravity%20CLI.md)"
---
Google's open-source terminal agent. Replaced by Antigravity CLI
for consumer tiers on 2026-06-18. See also [Claude Code](../Claude%20Code.md).

# Research/skill-catalog/markdown-db.yaml
markdown-db: 0
depends:
  harness-reference: { source: "github:osdlc/skillwright//harness-reference/corpora/beta" }

# Research/skill-catalog/skills/deploy.yaml
description: Deploy the current branch to staging.
runs_on:
  - "[[harness-reference/harnesses/Claude Code]]"
  - "[[harness-reference/harnesses/Gemini CLI]]"

# projects/Skillwright.md   (a note in the host vault, not in a corpus record)
---
publishes_to:
  - "[Claude Code](../Research/harness-reference/harnesses/Claude%20Code.md)"
---
Host notes may use any link form; Obsidian keeps them up to date.

steps.title: The root file: the spec version, then a front page
steps.summary: Frontmatter holds the data; the body is what a reader sees first in Obsidian.
steps.detail: Later versions may allow overrides here (a type folder whose name differs from the type, nested record folders). v0 has none.

steps.title: `x-ref` marks a field that holds a link
steps.summary: The value must resolve to a record of type `harnesses` in this corpus.
steps.detail: `x-ref` is a named keyword of the markdown-db vocabulary. Validators must register it; JSON Schema validators reject unknown keywords by default.

steps.title: A link inside the corpus is a relative Markdown link
steps.summary: In frontmatter it is a Markdown link inside a string; Obsidian 1.11.4+ treats it as a link in Properties.
steps.detail:
The path is relative to the file holding it. Spaces are written `%20` (or the target wrapped in `<…>` in the body). Every tool reads it the same way: GitHub, Docusaurus, VitePress, MkDocs, Obsidian, Foam, mdbase, OKF.

A bare path string (`successor: "Antigravity CLI.md"`) is **not** a link in any tool we tested, so the spec requires the `[text](path)` form.

steps.title: Body links use the same form
steps.summary: Standard CommonMark. No plugin needed in docs generators.
steps.detail: Tested: Obsidian rewrites these correctly when a record moves inside the corpus, and leaves them alone when the whole corpus moves.

steps.title: A corpus declares the corpora it links to
steps.summary: `depends` names another corpus, like a package dependency. Open design: see the mount question.
steps.detail: Cross-corpus links are the one case relative paths can't handle well, because they depend on where both corpora are mounted. Naming the dependency keeps the corpus byte-identical wherever it is mounted; `mount` records where each dependency lives.
steps.warning: Not settled. The mount and distribution design comes next.

steps.title: Cross-corpus links name the dependency
steps.summary: Written as a wikilink with the corpus name. Resolved through the mount table by our tools, and by suffix match in Obsidian.
steps.detail: This record is YAML, so no editor sees or rewrites its links; only `validate` checks them.

steps.title: Host notes outside any corpus are free
steps.summary: A vault note may link into a corpus any way it likes. Obsidian rewrote this link correctly when the corpus moved.
steps.detail: Only the host's own files change on a move. The corpus does not.

rungs.label: Relative Markdown link: `[X](X%20Y.md)`
rungs.detail: **Canonical inside a corpus.** Resolved from the file that holds it, literally. `validate` does not fall back to name matching, unlike Obsidian, so a broken path is always reported.

rungs.label: Dependency wikilink: `[[harness-reference/harnesses/X]]`
rungs.detail: **Canonical across corpora.** The first segment names a corpus listed in `depends`; the mount table says where it is. Obsidian resolves it by path suffix.

rungs.label: Any other wikilink: `[[X]]`, `[[harnesses/X]]`
rungs.detail: Accepted, not canonical. Resolved by unique path suffix; more than one match is an error. `validate --fix` rewrites it to the canonical form.

examples.label: Daily note → `[[Claude Code]]`
examples.note: Host note; in a record this would be an error, because the trap note makes it ambiguous.

blocks.title: Mini-apps and where to put corpora
blocks.text:
**Use case: an app keeps its data as a corpus in a vault.** A reading list, a task tracker, a set of inherited policies: an Obsidian plugin, CLI or small web app reads and writes records, and the user can still browse and edit them as notes. That adds four needs:

1. **Finding its corpus.** Users move and rename folders, so an app needs a stable handle: an optional `id` in the root file (`id: reading-list`, or a UUID). The app scans for `markdown-db.md` and picks the one with its id. The folder name stays the corpus's name for links.
2. **Writing records faithfully.** A writer changes only the keys it owns and keeps key order, unknown keys and the body. Same rule as rust-ontogen's `markdown-store` and mdbase.
3. **Concurrent edits.** v0: whole-file writes, last writer wins. Apps that need merging follow mdbase's merge profile.
4. **Upgrades.** A schema version and migrations: deferred, but the root file leaves room for them.

**Placement guidance (non-normative).** The spec lets a corpus sit anywhere; these are the recommended places:

- **In a vault:** one top-level folder for structured data (`Data/` or `_data/`), one corpus per app or dataset under it, named after it. Side by side, not nested.
- **In a code repository:** `corpora/<name>/`, as `harness-reference` does.
- **Don't** put a corpus inside another corpus's type folder.
- **Keep corpora that link to each other side by side** in one folder.

questions.prompt: How is a corpus root marked?

options.label: `markdown-db.md` (or `.yaml` / `.json`), data in frontmatter
options.detail: The name alone marks a corpus. The `.md` form is the corpus's front page in Obsidian. No clash with folder notes, no Hugo leaf-bundle issue.

options.label: `index.md` with `markdown-db: 0` in its frontmatter
options.detail: OKF-shaped and a landing page in docs generators. Detection must read frontmatter; common file name; Hugo treats it as a leaf bundle.

options.label: `markdown-db.yaml` only
options.detail: Unambiguous, but invisible in Obsidian and no front page.

options.label: No marker
options.detail: No boundary for nesting and no version check.

options.label: Its folder name
options.detail: Three-segment links work as plain path suffixes, in Obsidian too. Renaming the folder breaks links into it, like renaming a package.

options.label: A `name` in the root file
options.detail: Survives a folder rename, but Obsidian cannot resolve links by a declared name, so cross-corpus links would work only in our validator.

questions.prompt: Where does a type's schema live, and is it required?

options.label: Inside the type folder, named after it: `harnesses/harnesses.schema.md` / `.yaml` / `.json`
options.detail: Travels with its folder. The `.md` form shows the type as a note in Obsidian, with prose about it. JSON Schema editor tooling reads only the `.json` / `.yaml` forms.

options.label: Inside the type folder, `.json` only
options.detail: One form, full JSON Schema tooling; not visible in Obsidian.

options.label: `<type>.schema.json` beside the `<type>/` folder
options.detail: Revision 1's proposal.

options.label: A type note `_types/<type>.md`, as mdbase does
options.detail: Schemas gathered in one folder, apart from their records.

questions.prompt: What may an id look like?

options.label: Any portable file name (`Claude Code`)
options.detail: No `/ \ : * ? " < > |`, no `[ ] # ^ |` (they break wikilinks), no leading or trailing space or dot. Unique after NFC and case folding. A type may narrow it with `x-id-pattern`.

options.label: Lowercase slugs only (`claude-code`)
options.detail: Safe in URLs and shells, but less readable in Finder and Obsidian.

questions.prompt: Which link form is canonical inside a corpus?

options.label: Relative Markdown links
options.detail: Tested: keeps the corpus unchanged when it moves; native in GitHub and docs generators. Costs `%20` for spaces and frontmatter strings like `"[X](X%20Y.md)"`.

options.label: Two-segment wikilinks `[[harnesses/X]]`
options.detail: Tested: Obsidian rewrites them to vault paths when the corpus moves; GitHub and docs generators need plugins.

options.label: Both, neither canonical
options.detail: Most flexible; two spellings for one reference and no portability guarantee.

questions.prompt: How are links between corpora written?

options.label: Siblings + relative links: dependent corpora are mounted side by side; links are relative paths; `depends` lets tools check
options.detail: One link form everywhere, followed by GitHub, Obsidian and docs generators. Corpus files never change when the sibling group moves together. Costs a layout rule: linked corpora live in one folder.

options.label: Name a declared dependency: `[[harness-reference/harnesses/X]]` plus `depends`
options.detail: Our tools resolve it through the mount table and Obsidian by path suffix; GitHub and site generators cannot follow it at all.

options.label: Relative paths across corpora
options.detail: Work in every tool, but break when either corpus moves, and mounting would have to rewrite files.

options.label: Not in v0
options.detail: Closed corpora until the mount design is done.

questions.resolution: Deferred to the mount and distribution design. v0 does not define links between corpora.

questions.prompt: How does a corpus choose which record formats it allows?

options.label: `formats:` list in the root file, default `[md]`
options.detail: Markdown-only by default: every record is a note, fully browsable and kept up to date in Obsidian. A hybrid corpus declares `formats: [md, yaml, json]`: data-only records may sit beside notes, even in one type; ids stay unique ignoring the extension.

options.label: A named switch: `mode: notes | hybrid`
options.detail: Same two behaviours under friendlier names; less extensible.

options.label: Markdown only, no option
options.detail: Simplest; data-only records are `.md` files with an empty body.

options.label: Per type, by file extension (revision 1)
options.detail: No declaration; each type uses one format. Mixed corpora happen by accident rather than by choice.

questions.prompt: How should markdown-db relate to mdbase?

options.label: Own spec; borrow mdbase's path, collision and type rules with credit
options.detail: Keeps vault-wide resolution and whole-file records, which mdbase lacks. Propose cross-collection links to mdbase upstream.

options.label: A profile of mdbase
options.detail: Conformant mdbase collections plus conventions. Cross-corpus links would be invalid in mdbase tools.

options.label: Adopt mdbase as is
options.detail: No spec of our own. Loses cross-corpus links and YAML/JSON records.

questions.prompt: Should `validate` check relative paths literally, with no name fallback?

options.label: Yes, literally
options.detail: Catches the case Obsidian hides: a broken path it still resolves by name. GitHub and site generators would show it as dead.

options.label: Fall back to name matching, like Obsidian
options.detail: Fewer errors; broken links reach published sites.

questions.prompt: Should `validate --fix` rewrite accepted wikilinks to the canonical form?

options.label: Yes
options.detail: People can paste wikilinks in Obsidian; the corpus converges on one form.

options.label: No, report only
options.detail: Never edits files.

questions.prompt: What makes a folder a type, and where does free-form narrative go?

options.label: A folder holding `<its name>.schema.*` is a type; everything else is narrative
options.detail: Mirrors the corpus marker. Narrative lives in record bodies, the corpus front page, and any folder without a schema file (guides, essays, daily notes). An empty schema file makes an untyped type. Links from narrative into records are still checked.

options.label: The root file lists its types: `types: [harnesses]`
options.detail: One place to see every type; the schema stays fully optional. Moving or adding a type means editing the root file.

options.label: Every top-level folder is a type
options.detail: No marker needed, but narrative can only sit in record bodies or the root, and a vault root cannot be a corpus without its daily notes becoming types.

questions.prompt: Should the root file carry an optional stable `id`?

options.label: Optional `id`, for apps and correlation
options.detail: Lets an app find its corpus after the user renames or moves the folder. Links still use the folder name.

options.label: Required `id`
options.detail: Every corpus is correlatable, at the cost of one more thing to author.

options.label: No id; apps are configured with a path
options.detail: Simplest spec; apps break when the folder moves.
